{{Short description|German inorganic chemist and professor (born 1957)}}
{{COI|date=May 2019}}
'''Evamarie Hey-Hawkins''' is a German [[inorganic chemist]] and professor at [[Leipzig University]]. Her research is focused on main group and transition metal chemistry.

==Biography==
She received her diploma (1982) and doctoral degree (1983) at the University of Marburg, Germany, with Kurt Dehnicke. After stays at the University of Sussex, UK (1984/85), the University of Western Australia (1985/86) and the ANU (1986/87), she returned to Germany and completed her habilitation in Marburg (1988). From 1988 to 1990 she was a research associate at the Max Planck Institute for Solid State Research, Stuttgart. Evamarie Hey-Hawkins has been a Full Professor of Inorganic Chemistry at Leipzig University, Germany, since 1993.

==Research==
Her scientific interests comprise many aspects of structural and synthetic chemistry.  Much of her work focuses on main group compounds, especially phosphorus compounds.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Cyclooligophosphanes and Their Coordination Chemistry|author1=Eilrich, Volker |author2=Hey-Hawkins, Evamarie |journal=Coordination Chemistry Reviews|year=2021|volume=437|article-number=213749|doi=10.1016/j.ccr.2020.213749|s2cid=233551394}}</ref> She has also conducted research on bioactive boron compounds.<ref>{{cite journal|title=Carbaboranes as Pharmacophores: Properties, Synthesis, and Application Strategies|author1=Scholz, Matthias |author2=Hey-Hawkins, Evamarie |journal=Chemical Reviews|year=2011|volume=111|issue=11|pages=7035–7062|doi=10.1021/cr200038x|pmid=21780840}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|title=New Keys for Old Locks: Carborane-Containing Drugs as Platforms for Mechanism-Based Therapies|author1=Stockmann, Philipp |author2=Gozzi, Marta |author3=Kuhnert, Robert |author4=Sárosi, Menyhárt B. |author5=Hey-Hawkins, Evamarie |journal=Chemical Society Reviews|year=2019|volume=48|issue=13|pages=3497–3512|doi=10.1039/C9CS00197B|pmid=31214680|s2cid=195065563|doi-access=free}}</ref> She has authored more than 540 publications in refereed journals.<ref>{{cite journal|last1=Caminade|first1=A.-M.|last2=Hey-Hawkins|first2=E.|last3=Manners|first3=I.|author1-link=Anne-Marie Caminade|title=Smart Inorganic Polymers|journal=Chem. Soc. Rev.|year=2016|volume=45|issue=19|pages=5144–5146|doi=10.1039/C6CS90086K|pmid=27711697|url=https://research-information.bristol.ac.uk/en/publications/smart-inorganic-polymers(fa23f129-4bb2-4ecb-9481-5eebcb199e43).html|hdl=1983/fa23f129-4bb2-4ecb-9481-5eebcb199e43|s2cid=1979590 |hdl-access=free}}</ref>
